title: Biology Grade 10 Practice Questions 2015 (5 chapters combined)
description: Combined 5 chapter files (B2015_G10U1.json, B2015_G10U2.json, B2015_G10U3.json, B2015_G10U4.json, B2015_G10U5.json) into one exam. 20 total questions.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following sentences explains the traditional use of biotechnology's production of:
options: dairy products at household level.
insulin using transgenic bacteria.
vinger using industrial fermenter.
myco-proteins under a laboratory.
questions.explanation:
Traditional biotechnology involves the use of natural organisms and simple techniques to produce products like yogurt, cheese, and other fermented foods at home or small-scale settings.

 The other options involve modern or industrial biotechnology.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following sentences is correct about mitosis? It:
options: produces four different daughter cells from a single cell.
is the division of sex cells resulting in identical daughter cells.
produces half number of chromosomes from the original cell.
is the division of somatic cells to make identical daughter cells.
questions.explanation: Mitosis is the process by which somatic (body) cells divide to produce two daughter cells that are genetically identical to the parent cell and contain the full (diploid) chromosome number.

options: RR is 50%.
rr is 25%.
Rr is 25%.
RR is 75%.
questions.explanation: A cross between two heterozygous pea plants (Rr × Rr) produces the following genotypes in a Punnett square: Thus, the probability of offspring being homozygous recessive (rr) is 25%.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is correct about DNA? It is
options: single stranded molecule.
less stable and degrades quickly.
smaller molecule and coding for only protein.
made of phosphate, sugar and bases.
questions.explanation:
DNA (Deoxyribonucleic acid) is a polymer made up of monomers called nucleotides.

 Each nucleotide consists of three parts: a phosphate group, a deoxyribose sugar, and a nitrogenous base (A, T, C, or G).

questions.questionText: Which one of the following monohybrid crosses can be a test cross?
options: RR x Rr
Rr x Rr
RR x RR
RR x rr
questions.explanation:
A test cross is always performed by crossing an organism with an unknown genotype (usually dominant phenotype) with an organism that is homozygous recessive (rr).

 This allows a scientist to determine the genotype of the first organism.
 Among the options, RR x rr (crossing a homozygous dominant with a homozygous recessive) is a type of cross used in Mendelian genetics and fits the definition of crossing with the recessive parent (though Rr x rr is the most common test cross).

questions.questionText: In the nervous co-ordination system, which of the following statements explains the synapse? It is a:
options: part of the skull that encloses brain for the purpose of protection.
chemical that transmits nerve impulse across the nervous system.
short term change in the electrical potential on the surface of cells.
junction between two neurons or a neuron and a muscle.
questions.explanation: A synapse is the junction where a nerve impulse passes from one neuron to another neuron or from a neuron to a muscle cell, allowing communication within the nervous system.

questions.questionText: Two students want to demonstrate a simple spinal reflex action using the knee jerk reflex. One of them sits down with one leg loosely crossed over the other. The other hits the crossed leg just below the knee cap Gentle but  firmly using the edge of his hand. Which one of the following situations will happen during this demonstration? The:
options: hip ligament stretches the muscle
impulse travels to the brain.
impulse travels to quadriceps muscle from the brain.
lower leg will jerk downwards and inwards.
questions.explanation:
In the knee-jerk reflex (a simple spinal reflex), tapping the tendon below the kneecap stretches the quadriceps muscle.

 This stretch is detected by sensory neurons, which send an impulse to the spinal cord. The spinal cord immediately sends a motor impulse back to the quadriceps, causing the lower leg to jerk downwards and slightly inwards without involving the brain.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following eye structures is correctly matched with its function?
options: Iris - controls the amount of light entering the eye.
Pupil - serves as the eye's protective outer layer.
Choroid - bends the light into the eye.
Cornea - provides nutrition to the retina.
questions.explanation: The Iris contains muscles that constrict or dilate the pupil, thereby controlling the amount of light that enters the eye and reaches the retina.

questions.questionText: What is the function of dermis of the skin? It:
options: forms a waterproof around the body tissue.
contains blood vessels and sweat glands.
acts as protection against heat loss.
protects the entry of pathogens into the body.
questions.explanation: The dermis is the second layer of skin, characterized by a dense matrix of connective tissue that houses structures like blood vessels, hair follicles, and sweat glands.

questions.questionText: Children who play by spinning round and round fast, when they stop, they feel dizzy. Why?
options: The fluid in their semicircular canals keeps on moving after they stop.
The sensory hairs vibrate highly in response to movement of their body.
The otoliths round in the same direction with the head.
The optic nerves reports that the children are still moving.
questions.explanation:
Dizziness after spinning is caused by inertia affecting the endolymph fluid in the semicircular canals of the inner ear.

 When the body stops, the fluid continues to move for a moment, sending signals to the brain that the head is still rotating, leading to the sensation of dizziness.

questions.questionText: When does menstruation start in women with no obvious reproductive a health problem? It happens when
options: pregnancy occurs and the embryo obtains nourishment and oxygen.
the spongy lining of the uterus detaches in the absence of pregnancy.
the fertilized ovum reaches the uterus and attaches into the thick, spongy lining.
the FSH stimulates the development of a follicle in the ovary and the egg ripens.
questions.explanation:
Menstruation is the shedding of the thickened inner lining of the uterus (endometrium/spongy lining).

 This occurs specifically when there is no pregnancy, causing a drop in progesterone and estrogen, which triggers the detachment of the lining.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following sentences is correctly matched with the function of kidney structures?
options: Glomerulus - concentrates urine and conserves water
Loop of Henle - involved in ultrafiltration
Bowman's capsule - acts as a filter to produce urine
Cortex - monitors the osmotic pressure of the blood
questions.explanation: The Bowman's capsule surrounds the glomerulus and collects the fluid forced out of the blood, acting as the initial filter to produce urine (filtrate).

questions.questionText: Which one of the following temperature controlling mechanisms in homotherms is categorized into behavioral method?
options: Shivering as a result of drop in temperature
Seeking shade when the temperature rises
Sweating when the temperature increases
Constriction of capillaries when the temperature falls
questions.explanation:
Behavioral mechanisms involve voluntary actions.

 Seeking shade is a voluntary action used to reduce heat gain and thus control body temperature, classifying it as a behavioral mechanism. 

The other options (A, C, D) are physiological (involuntary) responses.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is NOT the function of the liver?
options: Storing glycogen
Controlling cholesterol
Bile formation
Monosaccharide metabolism
questions.explanation:
The liver functions include storing glycogen, controlling cholesterol levels, and forming bile.

 However, monosaccharide metabolism primarily occurs in the cells of the body (e.g., glycolysis in cytoplasm) rather than being a direct function of the liver.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements correctly describes the movement of materials in plants?
options: The transport of organic materials is due to transpiration.
Passive transport can take place in the pholem.
Active transport can take place in the xylem.
Water is transported in dead tissue.
questions.explanation:
Water is transported through the xylem vessels, which are composed of dead tissue (tracheids and vessel elements).

 Organic materials (sugars) are transported in the phloem, and their movement is active, not passive, and not primarily driven by transpiration (which drives water movement in the xylem).

questions.questionText: What will happen if an agriculture extension worker injects gibberellins into a dwarf plant? The:
options: stem will grow.
leaves will fall.
side shoots will grow fast.
roots will storages.
questions.explanation:
Gibberellins are plant hormones that promote stem elongation and cell division.

When an agriculture extension worker injects gibberellins into a dwarf plant, the hormone stimulates stem growth, making the plant taller.

The other options (leaf fall, side shoot growth, root storage) are not primary effects of gibberellins.

questions.questionText:
A biologist collected two types of seeds (SA and SB) from the field and sowed them in moist soils enriched with nutrients. Then, he recorded his observations as follows:

 SA
     The seedling of this seed emerged from the soil curved while pushing up through the soil.

 The hypocotyl straightened and carried the cotyledons and plumule above the soil surface.

 SB
     The plumule of the seedling pushed its way out of the soil, while the cotyledon remained underground.

     Unlike what occurred during the germination of SA, the plumule of this seed did not form a hook.

Which one of the following is correct about the observations of the biologist?
options: SA is of a monocot, while SB is of a dicot.
Both SA and SB are of monocots.
SA is of a dicot, while SB is of a monocot.
Both SA and SB are of dicots.
questions.explanation:
The observations describe two types of germination:

SA shows epigeal germination (cotyledons pulled above ground by the lengthening hypocotyl hook).
 This type of germination is typical of dicots (Dicotyledons).

SB shows hypogeal germination (plumule pushes straight out while cotyledons remain underground).

 This type is typical of monocots (Monocotyledons).

Therefore, SA is of a dicot, while SB is of a monocot.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an Ethiopian endemic plant?
options: Bahir zaf
Bunna
Noug seed
Avocado
questions.explanation:
Noug (Guizotia abyssinica) is endemic to Ethiopia, meaning it naturally grows only in this region.

 The other plants—Bunna (coffee), Bahir zaf, and Avocado—are found in multiple regions outside Ethiopia.

questions.questionText: Walia ibex is an endemic animal species in Ethiopia which is found in
options: Bale Mountain National Park.
Simien Mountains National Park.
Nechisar National Park.
Omo National Park.
questions.explanation: The Walia Ibex (Capra walie) is an endemic and critically endangered wild goat species found almost exclusively in the Simien Mountains National Park in northern Ethiopia.

questions.questionText: All of the following sentences are correct about pollution EXCEPT
options: burning fossil fuels increases pollution due to the release of hydrocarbons.
burning of wood increases pollution by causing global dimming which blocks sunlight.
deforestation increases the amount of CO₂ absorbed from the atmosphere.
decomposition of dead bodies increases the amount of CO₂ in the atmosphere.
questions.explanation:
The statement that deforestation increases the amount of CO₂ absorbed** is INCORRECT.

 Deforestation *decreases* the absorption of CO2 (because trees are carbon sinks), leading to a net *ncrease of CO2 in the atmosphere, which contributes to pollution (global warming).
